Programs

Discover through Advance.

A child needs a room, shared tools, and a coach. The ages are below. Ages 13–17 come through older partner schools.

$100 per child for a camp week is the participation goal.

The 2027 season in Dallas–Fort Worth scales the 2024 pilot to about 15 teams and about 90 students. See the 2027 season.

Get session updates

See sponsor goals

Three programs

AfroBot Academy

Kids learn to code and build with a mentor. Lessons are also at learn.afrobot.org.

AfroBot League

A team can start in one town, then meet teams nearby, then meet at a national event. A later meet between countries has no date yet.

AfroBot Innovation Lab

Kids try a prototype for a real problem, such as water or farming. They do not have to start a company.

Ages 6–9

Discover

Teams build a life-size vehicle by hand.

Ages 9–12

Build

Teams carry a life-size vehicle through a longer build.

Ages 13–17

Innovate

An AI agent is the brain of a humanoid robot.

Ages 13–17

Compete

Teams prepare humanoid robots for recognized robotics competitions.

See competitions

Ages 13–17

Advance

Older students mentor younger teams with an adult coach.

University pathways

The camp-week cost has a $100 goal.

A workshop a family can start

A child starts at a workshop, builds with a mentor, and can move toward a team. A $10 workshop is a hope, not today’s price.
